Tessa / team — first pass below. High-level proposal for HeliosAI (target: 6-month ramp to 1.5k concurrent seats):

1) Tranche plan (OEM + cloud backstop):
   - Tranche A (30% capacity) — OEM HW: 8xA100 units, ship target late Mar. Reserve with 25% deposit.
   - Tranche B (40%) — OEM HW: mix 8xA100 + 16xH200, ship target late Apr–May. Reserve 35% deposit.
   - Tranche C (30%) — cloud reserved capacity (AWS/GCP) to be contracted as a buffer for the first 90 days after go-live (hourly reserved instances + burst capacity).

2) Operational staging:
   - Build a 10% staging pool in our Dedicated region to accept early traffic and migration tests.
   - KV/prefix caching policy to reduce on-prem token cost during phased onboarding.

3) Risk & mitigation:
   - Customs/port: add a 14–21 day buffer to ship dates for east-coast routing.
   - If OEM slips >21 days, convert Tranche C cloud hours to firm reserved instances and re-prioritize customer routing to cloud for critical APIs.

Cost delta: initial estimate shows OEM-first approach reduces 6-month unit cost by ~18% vs cloud-first, but increases schedule risk. I included rough numbers in the attached MAP.

Next steps: Karthik — can you validate the staging pool sizing assumptions and the timeline feasibility with the infra team? If we agree, I'll propose the tranche ladder to Helios and ask Aurelie to confirm quote hold windows.

-Ben

Enterprise Sales — Redwood Inference
